passage:
Samir came in from the gate with his lower lip stuck out, dragging the toy truck behind him. Papa Yogesh looked up from the newspaper. "What happened, Samir?"
"Ayaan went home."
Yogesh set the paper down. "You are sad because Ayaan had to leave before you finished playing."
Samir looked at him. He nodded slowly. "Yes."
"That's a big sad."
Samir climbed into his lap. His shoulders dropped, and the lip went back in. After a while he said, "Can Ayaan come tomorrow?" "We'll ask his mother," said Yogesh.

qa.q: Who went home?
qa.a: Ayaan.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling, and what shows it?
qa.a: Sad. Samir came in with the lower lip out, dragging the truck, and nodded when Yogesh named the sadness.

qa.q: What did Yogesh do that helped Samir?
qa.a: Yogesh named the feeling, "You are sad because Ayaan had to leave before you finished playing," and let Samir climb into his lap.

qa.q: How might Yogesh have felt seeing Samir come in with the lip stuck out?
qa.a: Concerned and caring, and Yogesh put the paper down and gave full attention right away.

grounding: Yogesh names Samir's sadness about Ayaan leaving, and the child nods and calms; naming the feeling helps a small child feel understood.

passage:
"Kashish? What's wrong?" said Tarun, kneeling by the door.
Kashish's face was scrunched, arms crossed tight. "Nothing."
"You came in fast. Your face is red. I think you are angry because your paper boat got wet at school."
Kashish looked up. "It got all soggy!"
"You worked so hard on it, and it fell apart. That's a lot to be angry about."
"Yes." Kashish leaned into Tarun. "I made it blue."
"A blue boat, and it got soggy. That's really hard."
After a while, Kashish said, "Can we make another?"
"Yes, let's."

qa.q: What color paper boat did Kashish make?
qa.a: Blue.

qa.q: What was Kashish feeling when coming in fast with a red face?
qa.a: Anger and disappointment about the paper boat getting soggy at school.

qa.q: What did Tarun do that helped Kashish sort out the feeling?
qa.a: Tarun knelt down, named the anger and the reason, and repeated it in different words, until Kashish could say it out loud.

qa.q: How might Tarun have felt when Kashish first said "Nothing"?
qa.a: Concerned but patient, since Tarun stayed close and offered a guess about the feeling instead of pushing.

grounding: Tarun names Kashish's feeling and its cause, and the child nods, calms and can move on.

passage:
Kindergarten note, Monday.
Reena (5) sat in the corner at playtime, not playing. Her best friend Shreya moved to another school on Friday. Reena's lip was trembling. When I sat down beside her, she said nothing.
I said softly, "You're sad because Shreya isn't here anymore." Reena looked at me and nodded hard. Then she leaned against my arm and cried a little.
After a while she said, "I miss her." I said, "Of course you do. She was your good friend." Reena wiped her eyes and went to the sandpit. I'll ask her mother if a video call with Shreya might help.

qa.q: When did Shreya move to another school?
qa.a: On Friday.

qa.q: How did Reena feel when the teacher named her feeling?
qa.a: She felt understood, nodding hard and leaning on the teacher's arm to cry.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped Reena sort her feelings?
qa.a: The teacher named the feeling and its reason, 'You're sad because Shreya isn't here anymore', helping Reena feel understood.

qa.q: What might a video call mean to Reena?
qa.a: It might comfort her, letting her see that Shreya is still her friend.

grounding: Shows an adult naming a young child's sadness about a friend leaving, and the child nodding and calming.

passage: In the village near Kurnool, Noor, five, sat on the doorstep kicking at the dust. Her cousin Nitin had gone back to the city after the summer holidays. She wouldn't eat her lunch. Ammi sat beside her. "You're sad because Nitin went home, na?" Noor's lip wobbled. She nodded. "He was going to teach me marbles." "You miss him." Noor leaned on Ammi. "Yes." Ammi stroked her hair. After a bit, Noor sat up. "Can we call him later?" "Yes. After dinner." Noor ate her lunch.

qa.q: What was Nitin going to teach Noor?
qa.a: Marbles.

qa.q: How did Noor feel after Ammi named her feeling?
qa.a: She felt understood and calmer, leaning on Ammi and then eating her lunch.

qa.q: How did naming the feeling help Noor?
qa.a: It helped Noor sort out that she was sad because Nitin had left, and feel understood instead of scolded.

qa.q: How might Nitin feel when Noor calls him?
qa.a: He would probably feel happy that his little cousin misses him.

grounding: Shows a parent naming a young child's sadness about a cousin leaving, and the child nodding and calming.

passage: In their Singapore flat, Mei, four, stood at the window, crying, after her friend Diego went home from the playdate. She threw her toy bear on the floor. Her mother knelt down. "You're sad because Diego had to go home." Mei nodded, tears dripping. "And maybe a bit cross, because you were having fun." Mei nodded again, harder. Her mother picked up the bear and held it out. "It's okay to feel sad and cross." Mei took the bear and hugged it, and then hugged her mother.

qa.q: What did Mei throw on the floor?
qa.a: Her toy bear.

qa.q: What was Mei feeling at the window?
qa.a: She was sad and a bit cross because Diego had gone home.

qa.q: What helped Mei calm down?
qa.a: Her mother named both feelings and why, and said it was okay to feel them, so Mei felt understood.

qa.q: How might Diego feel about the playdate?
qa.a: Diego probably enjoyed it too, since Mei was having so much fun with him.

grounding: Shows a parent naming a young child's sad and cross feelings after a friend leaves, helping her feel understood and calm.

passage: At the daycare gate, Tarun would not put his shoes on. He kicked one across the mat and pressed his face into his cubby. Minakshi crouched beside him. The teacher whispered that Isha's family was moving to another city, and today was her last day. Minakshi rubbed his back. "You are sad because Isha left," she said quietly. "You wanted to play with her tomorrow too." Tarun lifted his face and nodded. His lip wobbled, then stopped. He fetched the kicked shoe himself. "Mumma, can we draw her a picture?" he asked.

qa.q: Why was it Isha's last day?
qa.a: Isha's family was moving to another city.

qa.q: How can you tell Tarun felt calmer after Minakshi spoke?
qa.a: He lifted his face and nodded, his lip stopped wobbling and he fetched the shoe himself, so he felt understood and less upset.

qa.q: What could Minakshi do next to help Tarun?
qa.a: She could say yes to drawing Isha a picture together, which gives his sadness something gentle to do.

qa.q: Why might the teacher's whisper matter to Minakshi?
qa.a: Without it, Minakshi might have seen only a child refusing his shoes; knowing about Isha let her name the real feeling instead of scolding.

grounding: Shows a parent naming a small child's sadness about a friend leaving, and the child nodding and calming.
